copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 brings Curaçao together with Côte d'Ivoire, scheduled for Thursday 25 June 2026 at 20:00 UTC. The Desk reads every priced match on Polymarket and Kalshi against an independent model number, then publishes a single verdict — Pick, Pass, or Avoid — with the math the call rests on. On this fixture that verdict is a Pick, on the Curaçao side.

The model starts from public Elo ratings: Curaçao on 1790, Côte d'Ivoire on 1740 — a 50-point difference in favour of Curaçao. Elo source: live for Curaçao, live for Côte d'Ivoire. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply on this fixture; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Run through the three-way split, the model reads: Curaçao to win at 42%, the draw at 27%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 31%. The three-way distribution carries the Desk's view of how often each outcome fires across the entire range of in-form-but-not-injured ninety-minute scenarios. It is not a forecast of the exact scoreline; it is a calibrated probability over the W / D / L resolution that Polymarket and Kalshi both settle on.

Polymarket's closing line: Curaçao to win at 28%, the draw at 29%, and Côte d'Ivoire to win at 55%. On the Curaçao side specifically, the market sits at 28%, which prices out at American odds of +264. The model has the same side at 42%. The gap across those two numbers — +14.2pp — is the basis for the Pick.

Our Pick gate uses a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior, the host bonus, and the altitude bonus across realistic ranges (±20 Elo, ±15 host, ±10 altitude) and reads the 5th-percentile value back out. On the Curaçao side, that lower bound is 34% — compared against the market's 28%, the lower-bound gap is +6.7pp. The Pick fires when that lower-bound gap clears +3pp; it does on this match. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so we're not claiming the market is generally wrong — we're claiming this particular side is mispriced on this particular fixture. Selection is the dimension this verdict is meant to add value on.

This number will move. Late-binding signals — confirmed starting elevens, injury updates, weather at the venue, suspensions carried in from previous fixtures — all re-enter the model on the data layer's late-binding cadence, currently weekly outside T-5d of kickoff, daily inside T-5d, hourly inside T-24h. A Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves the prior; we republish on every refresh. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade. The model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page; what to do with that is a reader's call.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Curaçao a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +14.2pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: A +14.2pp gap across model and market on the Curaçao side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Curaçao at 42%; Polymarket sits at 28%.
copy.title: Curaçao v Côte d'Ivoire · the model leans Curaçao
